ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and continuous screening of each general partner, limited partner, ultimate beneficial owner, authorized signatory, and TCSP filer against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List as applicable through Gibraltar Orders in Council, OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated wire transfers, Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit local risk flags, and INTERPOL notices. PEP verification is required at onboarding with quarterly re-screening; enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, adverse media, high-risk jurisdiction tax residency, or evidence of artificial entity-layer concealment. Screening evidence must be retained for a minimum of six years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registered names must be in English using Latin/Roman script. The statutory suffix 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'LP' must be the final element of the registered name. Non-Latin transliterations are not registrable as the legal name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not suggest Crown or Government patronage, a regulated financial activity, or a misleading connection with Gibraltar, the United Kingdom, or any public authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for a further 30 days upon written application made to the Registrar before the initial window expires. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must file a written Reconsideration Request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the refusal notice, attaching the official name search report and a memorandum distinguishing the name from cited conflicting marks. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may petition the Minister for Financial Services within 28 days of the reconsideration decision. Final recourse is an administrative-review application to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, to be filed within 42 days of the ministerial decision, on grounds of ultra vires, irrationality, procedural unfairness, or infringement of a legitimate expectation. Court application fees follow the prevailing Gibraltar Supreme Court Fees Order.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a standalone address for registration. The Limited Partnerships Act 2020 requires every limited partnership to maintain a registered office that is a physical, staffed location in Gibraltar, open during business hours for service of legal process. A remote or mailbox-only virtual office does not satisfy this requirement or the GFSC's integrity expectations for licensed TCSPs. For an unregulated 3D game art outsourcing ELP, the licensed TCSP's physical office may serve as the registered office and administrative address, with ancillary virtual conveniences such as meeting rooms and mail forwarding permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 30% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of registration. This reflects the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and the absence of a statutory license requirement. Desk-based reviews and TCSP-supervisory examinations are substantially more frequent than direct on-site inspections of the ELP premises; an unannounced site visit becomes materially more probable if the ELP claims economic substance in Gibraltar based on physical presence or headcount.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Gibraltar), ss. 1–15 (registration, statement of particulars, general and limited partner requirements); read with the Income Tax Act 2010, s. 8 and the Tax (Partnerships) Rules for pass-through eligibility; the Companies Act 1930 governs any corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Gibraltar, Registrar of Companies (administratively hosted within the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 — Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership and Statement of Particulars
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; contributions fixed by partnership agreement (USD 1 or as agreed); no escrow or deposit mandate with any Gibraltar authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, pursuant to the Limited Partnerships Act 2019, that: (1) the General Partner approves the Partnership Agreement as tabled, adopting its full terms; (2) the initial capital contributions of each partner, recorded in the capital account ledger, are hereby subscribed; (3) the Registered Office be fixed at the office address of the Licensed Registered Agent and the Licensed Registered Agent is appointed therefor; (4) the General Partner's authorised signatories are appointed as officers responsible for statutory filings; and (5) the General Partner is authorised to open bank or EMI accounts and execute all ancillary instruments to complete registration with the Companies Registry and the Income Tax Office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the 3D game art outsourcing activity is not a scheduled or licensable industry under Gibraltar law; no industrial operating permit is required, and no sectoral board approval applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating or manufacturing licence is mandated for digital creative services; a standard business registration and premises compliance suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (DESCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Minimal Risk — office-based digital services fall outside full EIA Schedule categories; an administrative environmental self-declaration is required only if physical lease premises exceed the permitted office threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or VOC emission thresholds applicable; domestic sanitary sewage discharges must comply with the Water Pollution Act 1999 and Gibraltar sewer discharge limits; electronic equipment waste disposed under the Gibraltar Waste Management Regulations (WEEE-aligned); energy performance certificate (EPC) required for any leased office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire risk assessment and means-of-escape certificate approved by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for any leased studio office; structural stability and building control clearance issued by the Gibraltar Building Control Office under the Gibraltar Building Act 2015; workplace occupancy and sanitary clearance from the Environmental Health Office; compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 1987 (as extended) including electrical safety certification and tax-compliant employment registration for studio staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Customs & Excise Department, HM Government of Gibraltar (VAT and indirect tax administration; e-services via the HM Government of Gibraltar tax portal) and the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (direct tax, Tax Reference Number and partnership registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Exempted Limited Partnership with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Limited Partnerships Act 2016; obtain the Companies House Gibraltar registration number (no minimum capital requirement). Step 2: File the Income Tax Office partnership registration application (Form GIB-ELP-TR) to obtain the partnership's Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) and to record the identities of all general and limited partners. Step 3: Confirm with the Income Tax Office the non-resident and non-Gibraltar-source status of the ELP to establish the exempt or tax-transparent position. Step 4: If taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold, submit a VAT registration application (VAT Form 001) to the Customs & Excise Department before commencing taxable activity. Step 5: Register for PAYES and Social Security contributions only if the ELP creates a local employment nexus; otherwise no payroll registration is required. Step 6: Open corporate bank/EMI accounts and file the known-beneficiary and source-of-funds dossier with the regulated payment institution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the Limited Partnerships Act 2016 and the Income Tax Act, an Exempted Limited Partnership may elect to be fiscally transparent, causing profits to be allocated to and assessed upon the partners directly in their own jurisdictions, instead of being taxed at entity level. Alternatively, the ELP may leave the default entity-level treatment in place or, where eligible, confirm full exemption from Gibraltar income tax for non-Gibraltar-source income. For United States-connected partners, a US federal check-the-box election (Form 8832) may classify the ELP as a partnership or disregarded entity for US tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections and notification requirements under Gibraltar's ATAD and OECD BEPS-aligned rules must also be assessed for any cross-border hybrid instruments used by the ELP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Gibraltar VAT or G-VAT, introduced under the VAT Act 2020 with effect from 1 January 2021 and modelled on the EU VAT Directive)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP 150,000 annual taxable turnover; compulsory registration applies as soon as the threshold is exceeded or will be exceeded in the next 30 days, and voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold where input VAT recovery is sought.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a mandatory B2B e-invoicing clearance regime; VAT invoices may be issued electronically or on paper. Invoices must contain the statutory content prescribed by the VAT Act 2020, including supplier name, address and TRN, recipient identification, description of supply, rate, and VAT amount. G-VAT returns must be filed quarterly through the Customs & Excise Department's online filing system, and supporting records, contracts and bank documents must be retained for at least six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% G-VAT rate applies to direct exports of physical goods to destinations outside Gibraltar and to cross-border supplies of services where the place of supply is treated as outside Gibraltar. For B2B supplies, the 3D game art and character rigging services supplied to overseas game developers, publishers or platform operators are zero-rated or outside the scope of Gibraltar VAT when the recipient is established in the United Kingdom or another non-Gibraltar jurisdiction, provided the recipient supplies a valid foreign VAT/TIN and the ELP holds contemporaneous evidence of the customer's overseas establishment; B2C supplies to private individuals resident outside Gibraltar are zero-rated where the service is effectively used and enjoyed abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD/EX1 where physical media or deliverables cross the customs frontier)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or courier consignment note evidencing physical export from Gibraltar
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign-currency settlement from the overseas client
Executed master service agreement and per-project work orders with the overseas game developer or publisher
Foreign customer VAT registration certificate or equivalent tax identification document confirming non-Gibraltar business establishment
Digital handover or delivery acceptance record substantiating the provision of 3D art, sculpting or rigging services
Zero-rated supply declaration signed by the overseas recipient where required by the Customs & Excise Department
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating claims expose the ELP to a civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT undercharged together with interest, a fixed penalty for overstated input VAT recovery, and retrospective assessments of up to six years under the VAT Act 2020. Dishonest evasion may be prosecuted criminally with fines and imprisonment. The Customs & Excise Department and the Income Tax Office may jointly claw back input VAT, issue disqualification orders against the general partner, strike the ELP from the registry, and render general partners jointly and severally liable for the fraudulent claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar - Currency Commission (the sole issuing authority for the Gibraltar Pound (GIP), which circulates at par with GBP). Prudential, conduct, and AML/CFT supervision of licensed banks and foreign-exchange counterparties is exercised by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC). There is no separate Gibraltar central bank; monetary stability is anchored by the Bank of England and HM Treasury, and the GFSC administers foreign-exchange licensing, sanctions screening, and cross-border payment oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar operates a fully convertible offshore financial centre. There is no exchange-control legislation and no regulatory distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility: export revenues from AAA-game 3D art outsourcing, partner capital contributions, intra-group loans, and profit distributions are all freely convertible between GIP, GBP, USD, and EUR. The GIP is pegged at par to GBP, and both currencies are legal tender in Gibraltar, materially reducing cross-currency settlement friction. Profit-remittance hurdles are practical rather than statutory: (i) banks apply enhanced due diligence to distributions flowing to a Cayman-domiciled ELP and will require audited accounts, CRS/FATCA returns, and a UBO declaration; (ii) the ELP must avoid being characterised as carrying on unlicensed deposit-taking or FX-dealing for third parties when converting client receipts; (iii) recurring high-value USD conversions require a documented hedging mandate to rebut any suggestion of speculative intent; and (iv) ultimate beneficial owners must be recorded in the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register. No Gibraltar withholding tax is imposed on ELP profit distributions, and no exchange-control certificate or central-bank approval is required for any remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Zero statutory surrender requirement, zero mandatory conversion ratio, and no fixed repatriation timeline for export proceeds. The ELP may hold export receipts indefinitely in USD, EUR, or GBP in multi-currency operational accounts, or in PayPal business balances within platform limits. As a service exporter under ISIC 7490, the ELP is outside any trade-related FX surrender regime. Prudent compliance practice, consistent with the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier, requires that all receipts above GBP 10,000 be traceable to signed client master service agreements and invoice schedules; that client-receivable accounts remain segregated from partner-capital accounts; and that USD-denominated export balances are marked to market monthly with any hedge instruments recorded at fair value in the ELP's pass-through accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (segregated ring-fence for the initial KY-ELP capital injection) and Operational Account (GBP, with USD/EUR multi-currency sub-accounts)
Operational Account (multi-currency GBP/EUR/USD) with dedicated capital-contribution ledger
Operational Account (GBP) and Capital Escrow Account (restricted to partnership capital calls)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM - permissible as an ancillary treasury rail but never as the primary banking anchor. UK-authorised electronic-money institutions (EMIs) may onboard the Gibraltar ELP remotely for GBP/EUR receipt collection and low-value contractor payouts, provided the ELP supplies a complete look-through of all partners along with certified partnership documents. Legal constraints: (i) post-Brexit, an FCA-authorised EMI does not automatically hold passporting rights into Gibraltar, so the service must be serviced from the UK without representing itself as a Gibraltar-licensed bank; (ii) most EMIs are structurally unwilling to service a Cayman-owned partnership as the sole bank, citing UBO opacity and sanctioned-jurisdiction exposure; (iii) EMI e-money balances are protected by safeguarding obligations, not by the Gibraltar Deposit Guarantee Scheme, so balances should be capped and swept daily to a regulated Gibraltar bank; and (iv) EMIs are unsuitable for commercial letters of credit, CHAPS same-day clearance, or high-value FX forward execution. A GFSC-licensed tier-1 bank remains mandatory for all regulatory and treasury-critical flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The corporate General Partner of the Gibraltar ELP, acting through its Gibraltar-registered agent and fiduciary, is generally required to attend an in-person KYC interview at the chosen bank; under current bank practice, a live video interview with the compliance officer may substitute if accompanied by original or notarised constitutional documents, a registered-office utility bill, and an introducer letter from the registered agent. Non-resident Limited Partners, including the Cayman indirect partner, are exempt from physical appearance provided each ultimate beneficial owner submits a certified passport, a recent bank reference, and a written source-of-wealth statement; certain banks additionally require a notarised identity attestation by a Gibraltar Notary Public. Fully remote opening with no local regulated introducer is not practicable for a Cayman-linked ELP, and banks will normally insist that at least one GP signatory maintain a physical presence or a statutory registered office in Gibraltar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman-registered ELP (KY_ELP) as direct or indirect owner of the Gibraltar ELP - international offshore-to-offshore structuring is a standard red flag under GFSC AML Guidance 2019 and FATF recommendation 25.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificates of registration of both the Cayman and Gibraltar ELPs; original partnership agreements with the full register of participants; consent letters from each general and limited partner; a group-structure chart disclosing all natural-person UBOs; CRS/FATCA self-certifications showing the tax-transparent status of each layer; three-source-of-wealth items, namely audited financial statements of the Cayman ELP, a bank reference for the KY-ELP, and the signed client pipeline for the 3D art outsourcing business; and a letter from the Gibraltar registered agent confirming the physical office and economic substance of the ELP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value cross-border revenue stream routed through PayPal alongside conventional wires - inconsistent with standard BPO treasury patterns and capable of masking third-party intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements and work-for-hire contracts with each named game studio; project work orders and art-delivery sign-off logs; an invoice schedule reconciled to PayPal settlement reports; PayPal business-account terms and periodic payout statements; a written treasury policy designating PayPal as a permitted operating rail; and a corporate no-cash policy prohibiting third-party receipt intermediation or crypto conversion of receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring USD-to-GBP/EUR conversion without demonstrable non-speculative hedging rationale - potential indicator of unlicensed FX-dealing or money-laundering through a pass-through entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and audit-committee minutes adopting an FX Hedging Policy with 100% underlying-exposure matching and zero net open position; forward and swap trades broken down to invoice-level exposure; an opinion from a GFSC-licensed service provider or chartered accountant confirming the ELP holds no client money; proof that all FX counterparties are GFSC-licensed or FCA/PRA-regulated banks; and a declaration that no conversion confers an economic benefit on the Cayman partner absent a valid inter-company services agreement and transfer-pricing file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax classification combined with profit distribution to a Cayman ELP - base-erosion and round-tripping indicators for the Gibraltar income tax administration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Income Tax Assessment Act returns evidencing the ELP's fiscal-transparency status and annual chargeability; audited statement of the ELP; a substance file satisfying the Income Tax (Substance Requirements) Regulations 2020, including the registered office lease, GP decision-making minutes, payroll and pension records, and bank signatory protocols; a transfer-pricing file documenting the arm's-length GP management fee and any inter-company charges; and CRS/GIPS returns demonstrating that no artificial tax advantage is being claimed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant primary route: the Cayman KY-ELP instructs its Cayman bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 wire in GBP or USD to the Gibraltar ELP's tier-1 Gibraltar bank account. The remittance information field must recite exactly: CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - KY_ELP TO GIBRALTAR ELP - PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT [DATE] - FISCALLY TRANSPARENT ELECTION - NO EXCHANGE CONTROL APPLICABLE. The receiving bank will require, before credit release, a certified copy of the Gibraltar ELP registration certificate, the executed limited partnership agreement, a GP capital-call resolution, the Cayman ELP's certificate of good standing, and UBO declarations from all natural-person partners. For statistical reporting, the transaction is classified as a capital-account transfer and, where a UK reporting bank is in the chain, as direct-investment other capital within the Bank of England survey. The injection must trace exclusively to partner reserve funds or a documented shareholder loan; commingling PayPal or client-receivable balances with the capital injection will trigger automatic enhanced due diligence. GBP injections are clearing-optimal because Gibraltar banks settle GBP via London nostro accounts using CHAPS and Faster Payments, whereas USD injections require US correspondent routing with higher fees and a 2-3 business-day clearing lag; USD amounts above GBP 1,000,000 equivalent should be split into tranches to remain below bank observation thresholds. No Gibraltar central-bank approval is required, but substance documentation must be retained to rebut any artificiality challenge.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursement hierarchy for trade settlements: (i) SWIFT MT103 priority wires in GIP/GBP, USD, or EUR for corporate vendors, tax authorities, and high-value subcontractors, with purpose narrative TRADE SETTLEMENT - 3D ART OUTSOURCING - INVOICE [REF] - ISIC 7490; (ii) UK CHAPS via the Gibraltar bank's London nostro for same-day GBP payments to HMRC, the corporate GP management fee, and UK-based artists; (iii) UK Faster Payments for urgent sub-GBP 1,000,000 disbursements, subject to recipient pre-validation and bank caps; (iv) SEPA Credit Transfers for EU partner studios and independent contractors, converting GBP to EUR at T+2; (v) irrevocable confirmed Commercial Letters of Credit issued by the tier-1 Gibraltar bank for enterprise infrastructure or game-engine licensing contracts above GBP 250,000, and for receivable settlement where a US client requires LC terms; and (vi) PayPal Business mass payouts for micro-royalties to individual 3D modelers and riggers, capped at GBP 50,000 equivalent per weekly batch and supported by a payout manifest. Every outbound wire must be backed by an invoice-and-acceptance evidence file; the GFSC AML/CFT rules require the bank to identify the commercial purpose of each charge, including recurring management fees to the Cayman partner, which must be underpinned by an executed inter-company services agreement and robust transfer-pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Clean/vanilla FX Forward (tenor 1M-12M, GBP/USD and GBP/EUR), fully matched to invoiced export exposure and the ELP's functional-currency requirements.
Cross-Currency FX Swap (GBP/USD and GBP/EUR) used solely for short-term liquidity rebalancing, with zero speculative overnight open positions.
GIP/USD Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) as an offshore net-settlement-only proxy for the Gibraltar-pound peg, permitted exclusively with a GFSC-licensed counterparty.
Zero-Cost Collar / Participating Forward, expressly non-speculative, requiring prior written approval of the bank's treasury desk and the ELP's audit committee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ELP Annual Return of the Exempted Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the registration anniversary date, being no later than 12 calendar months after the immediately preceding annual return date; no statutory grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fixed civil penalty of GBP 100, escalating to GBP 1,000 for continued default; persistent non-delivery for 12 months triggers administrative strike-off from the Gibraltar Register and dissolution of the ELP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Statement (UBO Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Secure Register (BOCR) via the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in parallel with the ELP Annual Return; any change in beneficial ownership must additionally be reported within 28 days of the underlying event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to GBP 5,000 per offence against the general partner and continuing daily default penalties; sustained default may lead to suspension of the partnership's register of partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CRS / FATCA Tax Transparent Filing (nil return where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June following the end of the calendar year under review for both CRS and FATCA reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties up to GBP 100,000 per offence under the Gibraltar CRS Regulations; FATCA non-compliance may additionally trigger referral to HMRC through the US-UK-Gibraltar intergovernmental arrangement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full independent statutory audit is mandatory where the ELP exceeds at least two of the three small-entity thresholds: annual turnover above GBP 6.5M, gross balance-sheet assets above GBP 3.26M, or more than 50 employees. Lower-volume ELPs may claim audit exemption only with the consent of 90% of the partners.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar-adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); Gibraltar-adopted UK GAAP (FRS 102) is also expressly permitted for small and medium-sized qualifying partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The ELP must maintain a full Register of Beneficial Owners and submit an annual confirmation to the Beneficial Ownership Secure Register simultaneously with the Annual Return. Any shareholding or partnership-interest transfer, disposal, or new beneficial owner achieving more than 25% interest or control must be evidenced and filed within 28 days; the annual confirmation re-certifies the standing data as accurate and current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors or General Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 per certified audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10% standard Gibraltar corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act (Cap. 123) and the Income Tax (Rates) Act); applied to the assessable profits of the Exempted Limited Partnership allocated to chargeable partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Pass-through classification: the ELP itself is not taxed at entity level; each partner bears tax only on its allocated share. Territorial/source-based taxation excludes foreign-source trading receipts of non-resident partners where no Gibraltar economic activity is performed. Patent Box regime: 50% deduction on qualifying game IP income (effective 5% rate on qualifying profits). Participation exemption for qualifying dividends and substantial shareholdings. No Gibraltar capital gains tax on share disposals outside anti-avoidance. Arm's-length outsourced artist commissions, cloud rendering costs, software licences, and production overheads are fully deductible.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act for trading losses carried forward against future profits of the same trade; relief can be restricted on a change in ownership coupled with a change in the nature of the trade).
